articles.title: South Sudan, Ethiopia and Rwanda rank among world's fastest-growing economies in 2026, outpacing Nigeria, South Africa, China and the US - Business Insider Africa
articles.summary: South Sudan, Ethiopia and Rwanda rank among world's fastest-growing economies in 2026, outpacing Nigeria, South Africa, China and the US  Business Insider Africa
articles.full_text:
- South Sudan's growth is driven by the recovery of its oil industry, while Ethiopia benefits from economic reforms and Rwanda from investments in construction, services, and tourism.
- Sub-Saharan Africa as a region is projected to outpace global economic growth, with an average of 4.5% in 2026 and 2027, compared to the global average of 3.1%.
- Rapid GDP growth percentages do not equate to economic size or wealth, and sustaining momentum will require diversification, increased investment, and improvements in household incomes.
According to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook, South Sudan leads Africa with projected real GDP growth of 10.5%, followed by Ethiopia at 9.2% and Rwanda at 7.4%.
The three countries occupy third, fourth and eighth positions, respectively, in a ranking of 18 selected fast-growing economies, reflecting different economic developments, from recovering oil production in South Sudan to reforms in Ethiopia and investment-led expansion in Rwanda.
Eight African countries feature in the ranking, highlighting the continent's growth potential despite persistent financial and political challenges.
What is driving growth in Africa's top three economies?
South Sudan's position largely reflects the recovery of its oil industry, which accounts for about 95% of exports and between 70% and 80% of government revenue.
The country's economy suffered a severe setback after fighting in neighbouring Sudan disrupted a pipeline carrying its crude oil to international markets.
According to the African Development Bank, South Sudan's GDP contracted by 27.6% in the 2023/24 financial year as oil production and exports collapsed.
With shipments recovering, the IMF expects economic output to rebound sharply, restoring some government revenue and foreign exchange earnings. However, much of this expansion represents a recovery from previous losses rather than growth across several industries.
South Sudan's heavy reliance on oil also leaves it vulnerable to renewed conflict, disruptions to export infrastructure and fluctuations in global petroleum prices.
Ethiopia's growth, meanwhile, follows a different path, supported by economic reforms, stronger exports, infrastructure development and expanding private-sector activity.
In July 2024, the government allowed the Ethiopian birr to trade more freely, introduced monetary policy reforms and secured IMF support as part of efforts to address foreign exchange shortages and restore economic stability.
These reforms have helped improve access to foreign currency, while coffee and gold exports have strengthened the country's foreign exchange earnings. Ethiopia has also opened sectors including banking and trade to greater foreign investment.
Despite these developments, inflation, external debt obligations and higher import costs continue to threaten household purchasing power and economic stability.
Rwanda's expansion is driven by construction, services, tourism and infrastructure investment as the country strengthens its position as a regional business destination.
According to the IMF, Rwanda's economy expanded by 9.7% in the first half of 2026, while stronger exports and remittance inflows helped narrow its external financing gap.
However, inflation reached 15.7% in August, reflecting domestic price pressures and higher international energy and fertiliser costs. Rwanda is also pursuing an IMF-supported financing programme to strengthen economic stability.
How Africa's fastest-growing economies compare with global powers
The IMF projects Nigeria's economy to expand by 4.2% in 2026, compared with 5.1% for Egypt and 1.0% for South Africa. South Sudan's projected growth is therefore more than twice Nigeria's rate and over ten times South Africa's.
Similarly, South Sudan, Ethiopia and Rwanda are expected to outperform major global economies, including China at 4.5%, the United States at 2.3% and the United Kingdom at 1.3%.
However, Guyana leads the global ranking with projected growth of 22.3%, largely driven by offshore oil production, followed by Taiwan at 10.7%, Vietnam at 8.4% and India at 7.0%.
Other African countries among the 18 selected fast-growing economies include Guinea at 7.2%, Benin, Niger and Sudan at 7.0% each, and Uganda at 6.2%.
Despite their higher growth rates, South Sudan, Ethiopia and Rwanda have much smaller economies than Nigeria, South Africa, China and the United States, highlighting the difference between rapid economic expansion and overall economic size.
For the three countries, sustaining growth will depend on attracting investment, creating jobs, diversifying production and improving household incomes.

articles.title: Beyond Diplomacy: How Tanzanians in Korea are building bridges of opportunity - Daily News
articles.summary: Beyond Diplomacy: How Tanzanians in Korea are building bridges of opportunity  Daily News
articles.full_text:
Beyond Diplomacy: How Tanzanians in Korea are building bridges of opportunity
TANZANIA: WHEN Tanzanians across Korea gather in the coastal city of Yeosu on 24 and 25 October this year, they will be celebrating more than a national occasion abroad. They will be marking 34 years of friendship between Tanzania and the Republic of Korea and showing how much of that friendship now rests on people, not just on governments.
Tanzania Diaspora Day 2026 will bring together Tanzanians living in Korea, representatives of government institutions, invited guests and friends of Tanzania in Yeosu, Jeollanam-do. Alongside culture, sport and community, the two-day event poses a forward-looking question: how can the growing Tanzanian community in Korea help open a new chapter of cooperation in education, employment, innovation, trade and investment?
The Embassy has organised the event with the Association of Tanzanians in Korea (TANROK) in recognition of the diaspora’s contribution to Tanzania’s development through remittances, investment, skills transfer and entrepreneurship. In 2024, remittances reached 2.116 tr/-, while diaspora investment through UTT-AMIS funds rose to 7.5 bn/-, up from 6.4 bn/- in 2023. With the right policies and support, that contribution can grow further.
Three Decades of Friendship
Since the establishment of diplomatic relations in April 1992, Tanzania and Korea have built strong ties based on mutual respect and shared development goals. Cooperation now spans infrastructure, education, healthcare, technology, trade, investment, tourism and culture.
Momentum grew in June 2024, when Dr. Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of the United Republic of Tanzania, visited Korea for the inaugural Korea–Africa Summit. Among the outcomes was a framework providing up to USD 2.5 billion in concessional financing through Korea’s Economic Development Cooperation Fund (EDCF) for 2024–2028.
Yet people remain at the heart of the relationship. Tanzanian students at Korean universities, public officials on capacity-building programmes, researchers and entrepreneurs all strengthen ties in ways formal diplomacy cannot. Their friendships and networks bring our two societies closer, and Diaspora Day is a chance to celebrate them.
Yeosu Comes Alive
Yeosu, with its maritime heritage and international outlook, is a fitting host for a celebration of connections across borders. Alongside cultural performances celebrating the heritage of Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, the programme will feature information clinics connecting the Tanzanian diaspora with public and private Tanzanian institutions and service providers on immigration, taxation, ports and logistics, banking and investment. There will also be room for open dialogue between the Embassy and the diaspora on welfare, careers, business and continued engagement with home.
Sport will also feature prominently, with planned friendly matches between Tanzanian participants, neighbouring African diaspora communities and youth teams. The highlight will be a match between Tanzania’s Under-17 national team, the Serengeti Boys, and Yeosu Marine FC U-18, a reminder that sport is a universal language that brings people together.
The Diaspora as a Bridge
The Tanzanian community in Korea, estimated at around 400 people and comprising students, researchers, professionals, entrepreneurs and families, is an important asset for both countries. Because they understand both societies, diaspora members are well placed to link businesses, universities, research institutions and communities.
They can introduce Korean investors to opportunities in Tanzania, promote Tanzanian products and tourist destinations, support academic exchanges and build partnerships in technology and entrepreneurship. Their knowledge of Korea’s business environment can also feed back into Tanzania’s development through mentorship, knowledge transfer and investment.
That is why we see the diaspora not merely as citizens living abroad, but as partners in economic diplomacy. The Embassy is committed to deepening engagement with Tanzanians in Korea, improving access to information and backing initiatives that connect their expertise with opportunities at home.
Just as important are the everyday encounters in classrooms, workplaces and neighbourhoods, where Tanzanians introduce their culture and aspirations to Korean society. These people-to-people ties are the foundation on which diplomatic and economic partnerships grow and prosper.
From Scholarships to Skills
Education has long been at the core of Tanzania–Korea cooperation. Through the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), Korean universities and other institutions, Tanzanian students, officials, researchers and professionals have benefited from scholarships, postgraduate study and technical training.
Korea’s support also reaches infrastructure, healthcare and institutional capacity-building. According to Tanzania’s Ministry of Finance, KOICA had provided approximately USD 139.5 million in grants under a cooperation programme established in 2014, as reported in March 2024. The EDCF, meanwhile, finances major development projects under the USD 2.5 billion framework.
The lasting value lies beyond the numbers, in the knowledge, expertise and networks these programmes create. Tanzanian beneficiaries gain exposure to advanced technologies and to Korea’s own experience of industrial transformation.
As we celebrate Diaspora Day, we extend heartfelt appreciation to KOICA, Korean universities and other development partners for their contribution to building Tanzania’s human capital. The next step is to link scholarships and training more closely with research, innovation, industry and skilled employment, so that both nations continue to benefit. In this regard, Tanzania commends the Korean government’s decision to extend the D-10 job-seeker visa for graduates of Korean universities from two years to a maximum of three.
Connecting Talent with Opportunity
Skilled employment is a promising new frontier. Korea’s ageing population and labour shortages in some industries have raised demand for international talent, while Tanzania has a growing pool of skilled professionals in engineering, information technology, healthcare, research, digital services and technical trades.
During President Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan’s 2024 visit, Tanzania expressed interest in labour cooperation through Korea’s Employment Permit System (EPS). Building on this, the two countries could pursue structured dialogue on professional visas, skills recognition, Korean-language training and partnerships between employers, universities and technical institutions, in line with Korea’s immigration and labour regulations.
Such cooperation should do more than fill vacancies. Korean employers would gain qualified professionals; Tanzanian workers would gain international experience and expertise that benefit their careers and their country. Any arrangement must be guided by verified labourmarket demand, transparent recruitment, fair working conditions and strong protection of workers’ rights.
ALSO READ: Govt raises bar on building safety, quality
Empowering the Next Generation
Young people must be at the centre of this agenda. Tanzanian graduates and professionals need the skills, language proficiency and practical experience to compete in Korea’s evolving labour market. Partnerships among universities, research institutions, training centres and businesses could open doors to internships, exchanges and joint research, within safe, transparent and lawful pathways.
The diaspora can help through mentorship, networking and support for newly arriving students and professionals. The Embassy, working with Tanzanian and Korean institutions, will continue to build practical partnerships that help young people realise their potential.
Looking Ahead
Diaspora Day 2026 will be more than a celebration of identity, culture and community. It is a platform to strengthen connections, engage with institutions from home, recognise Korea’s longstanding contribution to Tanzania’s development and explore how 34 years of friendship can inspire new partnerships in innovation, skills and employment.
I look forward to joining our diaspora community in Yeosu. I encourage every Tanzanian in Korea to take part, celebrate our shared heritage, strengthen their networks and find ways to contribute to Tanzania’s development.
I equally invite Korean institutions, universities, businesses, employers and development partners to keep building meaningful partnerships with Tanzania.
Tanzania–Korea relations will be strengthened by our people, enriched by our cultures and sustained by the opportunities we create together for future generations. Let us each play our part.

articles.title: Kenya and China reaffirm Transport Infrastructure partnership at Beijing Forum - Mjengo Hub
articles.summary: Kenya and China reaffirm Transport Infrastructure partnership at Beijing Forum  Mjengo Hub
articles.full_text:
Kenya and China have reaffirmed their strategic partnership in developing transport infrastructure to support regional trade and economic growth. Cabinet Secretary for Roads and Transport Davis Chirchir made the announcement during his address at the 2026 Financial Street Forum in Beijing.
Speaking at the annual conference, Cabinet Secretary Chirchir emphasised that transport network expansion remains central to attracting foreign investment across East Africa. The bilateral engagement highlights ongoing diplomatic efforts to secure long-term funding models for critical national transit routes.
Infrastructure development across Kenya has relied heavily on international capital partnerships over the past decade. Major arterial road networks and transit corridors continue to require sustained capital injection to maintain operational efficiency.
The Ministry of Roads and Transport maintains that public infrastructure projects must align with broader regional integration objectives. Delegates at the Beijing summit discussed sustainable financing mechanisms tailored for major capital development projects across emerging markets.
Kenya continues to evaluate diverse funding frameworks to support major civil engineering initiatives without overextending national debt thresholds. Further negotiations regarding specific project allocations are expected to continue between technical delegations from both countries.

articles.title: Egypt Highlights 23% Share of Intra-COMESA Exports, Reaffirms Commitment to African Integration - DNE Africa
articles.summary: Egypt Highlights 23% Share of Intra-COMESA Exports, Reaffirms Commitment to African Integration  DNE Africa
articles.full_text:
Egypt accounted for 23% of total intra-regional exports within the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) in 2025, Deputy Foreign Minister for African Affairs Mohamed Abu Bakr said, highlighting Cairo’s commitment to expanding regional trade and advancing economic integration across the continent.
Abu Bakr made the remarks during the 25th COMESA Summit in Harare, Zimbabwe, on October 22, as leaders from member states discussed ways to deepen economic cooperation and strengthen trade ties across the regional bloc.
Held under the theme “One Market, One Future,” the summit focused on advancing regional integration and unlocking opportunities to expand trade among member states.
The meeting also marked the transfer of COMESA’s chairmanship from Kenya to Zimbabwe, with Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa opening the summit.
According to Egypt’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Abu Bakr reiterated Cairo’s support for COMESA and efforts to establish a more integrated African market. He also affirmed the importance of strengthening coordination among COMESA, the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) under the tripartite free trade arrangement, alongside the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).
He called for closer cooperation among African countries to address mounting geopolitical and economic challenges, particularly those affecting maritime security, trade routes, market stability and supply chains.
Egypt Reaffirms Positions on Sudan and Somalia
During the 21st Meeting of COMESA Ministers of Foreign Affairs, Abu Bakr reiterated Egypt’s support for Sudan’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, as well as the preservation of its national institutions. He also underscored the importance of regional and international efforts to resolve the conflict, including the Quad and Quintet mechanisms.
On Somalia, the Egyptian official reaffirmed Cairo’s support for the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, highlighting Egypt’s participation in the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM).
The discussions also addressed the implications of shifting geopolitical dynamics for Africa’s energy security and economic prospects, underscoring the need for stronger continental coordination to respond to shared challenges.
Abu Bakr highlighted Egypt’s efforts to promote African economic cooperation through initiatives and platforms, including the Alamein Africa Business Forum, which aims to strengthen commercial ties and encourage investment across the continent.

articles.title: Egypt signs MoU to study regional logistics hub at Alexandria’s Dekheila Port - Urban & Transport - Egypt - Ahram Online
articles.summary: Egypt signs MoU to study regional logistics hub at Alexandria’s Dekheila Port - Urban & Transport - Egypt  Ahram Online
articles.full_text:
Egyptian Transport Minister Kamel Al-Wazir witnessed the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on Thursday to study the establishment of a regional logistics and re-export hub measuring 273,008 square metres at Alexandria’s Dekheila Port, the ministry said.
The hub, planned in the port’s western hinterland, would shift Dekheila from receiving ships and handling cargo to trade and value-added logistics.
The project comes as Egypt seeks private-sector partners to develop the country into a transit hub for the eastern Mediterranean. Al-Wazir called on the signatories to meet more frequently to prepare and sign an agreement setting out the terms and conditions before work begins.
The Alexandria Port Authority, Hassan Allam Utilities, and Al-Tarek Capital for Real Estate Asset Management signed the MoU. Ihab Salah, head of the port authority, and Amr Allam, co-CEO of Hassan Allam Holding and chairman of Hassan Allam Utilities, signed the document.
Al-Wazir said the deal implements President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi’s directives to make Egypt a regional hub for transport, logistics, and transit trade. He added that it also follows directives to deepen partnership with the private sector in investment and service projects.
The project aims to attract new logistics investment at Dekheila, the minister said. It would offer storage, handling, distribution, re-export, and final processing of products and light industries.
These services would add value to goods, improve services for exporters and importers, and help the port draw regional and international trade flows.
Al-Wazir said integrated logistics centres are a key pillar of the ministry’s plan to increase ports' economic returns. The plan would turn them from ship-receiving and cargo-handling points into integrated trade and logistics centres, strengthening Egypt’s position in the eastern Mediterranean.
Allam said transport and logistics are “one of the main pillars” of his group’s investment strategy. “We see promising opportunities to boost integration between ports, distribution networks, and industrial activities, raising the efficiency of cargo movement and opening wider access to markets for companies,” he said.
The Dekheila hub, he added, “embodies this approach” because of its connection to the port and the value-added services it would provide. He said the project would support more efficient supply chains and strengthen Egypt’s position as a regional transport hub.
The signing comes eight days after Al-Wazir inaugurated the EGP 700 million Al-Amriya Dry Port in Alexandria. The 146,000-square-metre inland facility is meant to ease congestion at seaports and cut transport costs.
Alexandria and Dekheila ports handle about 60 percent of Egypt’s foreign trade, according to government figures. Al-Wazir and his French counterpart Philippe Tabarot toured the Tahya Misr container terminal at Alexandria Port on 8 September. The terminal has handled 2.5 million containers since opening, the ministry said.
Container traffic is also rising. Egypt Maritime Ports Company handled more than 500,000 twenty-foot equivalent units in the first half of 2026, up 22 percent year-on-year, the ministry said in July.

articles.title: US-backed group Congo mines deal with Glencore in ‘final phases’ - Mining.com
articles.summary: US-backed group Congo mines deal with Glencore in ‘final phases’  Mining.com
articles.full_text:
A US government-backed group has nearly completed the acquisition of stakes in Glencore Plc’s copper-cobalt mines in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to a senior figure in the consortium.
Orion CMC was set up a year ago as a tool in the push by the US and allies to secure minerals deals around the world, targeting an eventual pool of $5 billion. In February, the venture announced a preliminary deal to purchase 40% of Glencore’s majority interests in a pair of major operations in Congo.
That transaction is in its “final phases,” Oskar Lewnowski, chief executive officer of specialist mining investor Orion Resource Partners, said in an interview on Bloomberg Television with Francine Lacqua. His firm was one of Orion CMC’s three founders alongside the US International Development Finance Corp. and Abu Dhabi’s L’imad Holding.
Saudi Arabia is also involved in Orion CMC, according to Lewnowski, who said he’s talking to “Asian allies” about joining the consortium. The venture aims to reduce dependence on China for a range of mineral products.
“We’re not looking to compete with China,” said Lewnowski. “We’re just looking to create a supply chain that doesn’t allow for monopolistic behavior by any one country.”
The executive said Orion CMC is advancing a deal to make an equity investment in Lifezone Metals Ltd.’s Kabanga nickel project in Tanzania, which was first reported by Bloomberg News in August. He said the group is also pursuing mining deals in Canada, Indonesia and Vietnam.
A transaction to back Chemaf SA, a copper-cobalt miner in Congo that’s been acquired by the US’s Virtus Minerals Inc., “is still possible” but Orion CMC is focused on closing the Glencore deal, according to Lewnowski.
Congo is the world’s second-biggest copper producer and largest source of battery metal cobalt. Chinese firms dominate output of both metals, which are often mined together in the central African country.
Copper traders are fixated on whether President Donald Trump will eventually move ahead with his proposals to place tariffs on imports. The administration is “fairly divided” on that question, said the Orion CEO.
But if tariffs don’t happen, “I think the US government probably takes a hard look at buying significant amount of tonnage that’s already in the United States and storing it.”
(By William Clowes and Francine Lacqua)

articles.title: Kisumu SGR Extension Project Advances Kenya’s Railway Link to Uganda as Cost Rises by Ksh148 Bn - Construction Review
articles.summary: Kisumu SGR Extension Project Advances Kenya’s Railway Link to Uganda as Cost Rises by Ksh148 Bn  Construction Review
articles.full_text:
Kenya’s KSh651 billion Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) extension from Naivasha through Kisumu to Malaba is advancing under a revised infrastructure financing plan, with the project designed to connect western Kenya to the Port of Mombasa and strengthen regional freight transport.
The Kenyan government plans to extend the Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) to Kisumu and Malaba on the Ugandan border. The National Treasury revised the budget for the wider Naivasha–Kisumu–Malaba extension to approximately KSh651 billion in October 2026. This is about KSh148 billion higher than the earlier estimate of KSh502.9 billion.
Project Developer and Main Contractors
The railway project is being implemented through Kenya Railways Corporation (KRC), under the Ministry of Roads and Transport. China Communications Construction Company (CCCC) and China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) have been identified as the Chinese companies involved in delivering the extension.
President Ruto Launches Kisumu SGR Construction
President William Ruto officially launched the project in March 2026. Construction activities on the Naivasha–Kisumu section were formally commenced in July 2026. The railway is intended to extend Kenya’s modern rail network beyond Naivasha. This is where the existing SGR currently terminates. The extension will then establish a connection with western Kenya and the Uganda border.
The Kisumu SGR development is expected to improve cargo movement along the Northern Corridor. This will connect the Port of Mombasa with inland commercial centres and neighbouring landlocked markets. The revised KSh651 billion budget, however, places financing at the centre of project delivery. The government is also considering revenue security and private-sector participation to support the capital-intensive railway expansion.
Naivasha–Kisumu–Malaba SGR Extension Project Scope and Railway Alignment
The Naivasha–Kisumu–Malaba SGR extension is divided into two main construction phases.
Phase 2B covers 264 kilometres from Naivasha to Kisumu. It also includes an 8.69-kilometre branch line to the proposed Kisumu Port on Lake Victoria. Phase 2C extends 107 kilometres from Kisumu to Malaba, near the Kenya–Uganda border. Together, the main railway sections account for 371 kilometres. However, the National Treasury’s latest reported budget indicates the Kisumu SGR as a 369-kilometre extension project.
The railway corridor passes through areas of Nakuru, Narok, Bomet, Kericho, Nyamira and Kisumu before continuing towards the western border region. The broader route is intended to improve rail access to agricultural, industrial and commercial centres. This is while supporting the movement of freight towards Uganda and other East African markets.
The proposed Kisumu branch line is also an important component because it is intended to connect the railway with the lakeside port. The connection could also support the transfer of cargo between rail and lake transport. This is however subject to the development of the port facilities and the availability of compatible freight-handling systems.
Additionally, the extension follows the completion of the Mombasa–Nairobi railway in 2017. The Mombasa-Nairobi railway was followed by an extension from Nairobi to Naivasha. The western section remained incomplete for several years after earlier financing arrangements failed to support continued development.
Kisumu SGR Extension Project’s KSh651 Billion Budget and Financing Structure
The latest project cost estimate stands at KSh651 billion, up from KSh502.9 billion. The KSh148 billion increase represents a substantial revision to the expected capital requirement for the remaining railway sections. KSh618.8 billion is expected to come from external financiers. Moreover, the exact financing arrangements and the mobilisation of the full amount have not been conclusively made public by the government.
The government has also been considering securitisation of future Railway Development Levy (RDL) collections. The levy is charged on imported goods. It is expected to provide a revenue stream that can support railway development. Under a securitisation arrangement, expected future revenue can be used to support financing raised through special-purpose vehicles or other approved structures.
The Government of Kenya has also previously indicated that it could raise up to KSh390 billion through bonds backed by future RDL collections.
A further element of the financing strategy involves separating railway infrastructure construction from the procurement and provision of rolling stock. Roads and Transport Cabinet Secretary Davis Chirchir has also previously outlined plans for private-sector participation. The private sector will mainly be involved in supplying locomotives, passenger coaches and freight wagons. The investors will potentially recover their investment through railway operations and freight charges. However, the final operating and concession arrangements remain subject to confirmation.
Construction Progress and Land Acquisition
Construction of the Naivasha–Kisumu–Malaba extension was formally launched in March 2026. This was followed by the commencement of works on the Naivasha–Kisumu section in July. Kenya Railways reported that the contractor placed the first rail and sleepers in Narok on July 1 and continued the commencement activities on July 2.
Land acquisition also remains a major implementation requirement. The National Land Commission has been involved in identifying affected properties. NLC has also been involved in coordinating the compensation process along the proposed corridor. More than 5,000 acres have been identified for acquisition for sections of the western SGR extension. Affected landowners also expect to receive compensation in accordance with applicable law.
Additionally, the project requires completion of environmental and social safeguards. This includes environmental and social impact assessment requirements and resettlement planning. These measures are important for managing the effects of construction on communities, property owners and the environment.
Other major construction activities will include railway earthworks, bridges and culverts, track installation and drainage systems. Stations, signalling, telecommunications and associated railway infrastructure also feature in the development plans.
Expected Impact on Kisumu and Regional Trade
The Kisumu SGR section is expected to improve access to rail freight and passenger services in western Kenya. By connecting the region to Naivasha and the wider SGR network, the project could provide an alternative to road transport for suitable freight and passenger journeys.
The proposed Kisumu Port branch line could also create opportunities for integrating rail and lake transport. Such integration would also depend on the development of port facilities, cargo-handling infrastructure and operational arrangements between railway and lake transport services. More inland, the Government of Kenya is also supporting trade and connectivity with projects such as the new KSh7.5 billion Nithi Bridge realignment project in Eastern Kenya.
At the national level, the extension is intended to improve freight movement from Mombasa towards western Kenya and Uganda. More reliable rail transport could help reduce pressure on highways, improve cargo logistics and support regional trade along the Northern Corridor.
The railway could also encourage investment in logistics centres, warehouses, industrial facilities and commercial developments near stations and freight terminals. However, the scale of these benefits will depend on actual cargo demand, service frequency, operating costs and the completion of connecting infrastructure.
Naivasha–Kisumu–Malaba Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) Extension Project Fact Sheet
Location: Kenya, extending from Naivasha through Kisumu to Malaba on the Uganda border.
Project type:Standard-gauge railway infrastructure.
Owner:Government of Kenya.
Implementing agency: Kenya Railways Corporation.
Supervising ministry: Ministry of Roads and Transport.
Main contractors: China Communications Construction Company (CCCC) and China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC)
Total main-line extension: 369 kilometres according to the latest Treasury budget.
Phase 2B: 264 kilometres from Naivasha to Kisumu.
Kisumu Port branch: 8.69 kilometres.
Phase 2C: 107 kilometres from Kisumu to Malaba.
Latest budget: KSh651 billion.
Previous estimate: KSh502.9 billion.
Expected external financing: Ksh618.8 billion
Funding strategy: Government financing and proposed revenue securitisation. Possible private-sector participation in rolling stock and operations.
Construction commencement: Official launch in March 2026. Initial construction works on the Naivasha–Kisumu section started in July 2026.
Construction status: Initial construction activities underway

articles.title: Nigeria and Egypt, alongside two other African countries, record the highest number of migrants turned away from Italy - Business Insider Africa
articles.summary: Nigeria and Egypt, alongside two other African countries, record the highest number of migrants turned away from Italy  Business Insider AfricaThousands of African asylum claims rejected in Italy  Townpress Newspaper
articles.full_text:
- African nationals, particularly from Morocco, Egypt, Tunisia, and Nigeria, faced very high asylum rejection rates in Italy in 2025.
- Moroccan applicants saw 90% of their decisions rejected, while Egypt and Tunisia experienced rejection rates of roughly 83% and 85%, respectively.
- Nigerian applicants had a 65% rejection rate, though some did obtain refugee status, subsidiary protection, or special protection.
- Italy issued over 104,000 first-instance decisions in 2025, with an overall protection rate—including special protection—of 30%.
The data reveal a difficult reality for people hoping to secure protection in one of Europe's major migrant destinations: submitting an asylum application does not guarantee the right to stay.
Italy recorded 9,485 asylum applicants from Morocco in 2025. Authorities made 6,315 decisions on applications from Moroccan nationals, rejecting 5,695 of them.
For Morocco’s fellow North African state, Egypt, 10,685 decisions involved Egyptian applicants; 8,900 were rejections, equivalent to roughly 83%.
Tunisia's figures were also stark: 5,035 of 5,895 decisions were rejected, a rate of about 85%.
DON’T MISS THIS: 2 African countries listed as UK lawmaker promises to end immigration from the Third World and ‘discriminate’
The figures suggest that applicants from these three North African countries faced particularly high rejection rates among the nationalities listed in the database.
Over in West Africa, Nigeria, one of Africa's largest countries by population, also featured in the figures. Italy recorded 3,385 Nigerian applicants in 2025, while 3,390 decisions were made on Nigerian cases.
Of those decisions, 2,220 were rejections, representing approximately 65%, as seen in the Asylum Information Database Italy report.
For the West African country, authorities granted refugee status in 660 cases, subsidiary protection in 55, and special protection in 460.
These figures show that, although rejection was the most common outcome among the decisions recorded, some applicants successfully obtained protection.
Morocco, Egypt, Tunisia and Nigeria were not alone. Georgia, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh also recorded high rejection rates in the table, although the figures cover countries beyond Africa and should not be treated as a complete picture of Italy's asylum system.
A difficult year for asylum applicants
Across Italy, authorities issued 104,560 first-instance decisions in 2025, with the overall protection rate, including special protection, standing at 30%, according to the report.
Italy registered 126,635 first-time asylum applications during the year, down from 151,120 in 2024.
Yet the 2025 figure was still almost double the 77,200 applications recorded in 2022.
The data, however, do not establish why individual claims were rejected, and a rejection does not by itself prove that an applicant's circumstances were illegitimate.
Ultimately, the figures offer a snapshot of the challenges facing asylum seekers, as Italy continues to process large numbers of claims while determining who qualifies for protection under its laws.

articles.title: Kenya Railways and NLC inspect Naivasha-Kisumu-Malaba SGR route - Mjengo Hub
articles.summary: Kenya Railways and NLC inspect Naivasha-Kisumu-Malaba SGR route  Mjengo Hub
articles.full_text:
Implementation activities for the proposed Naivasha-Kisumu-Malaba Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) project have moved forward following field assessments along the corridor. A technical delegation led by Engineer Tobias Otieno from Kenya Railways Corporation (KRC) joined officials to assess ground conditions.
The joint exercise included Commissioners from the National Land Commission (NLC), who accompanied the engineering team during the site visit. Officials reviewed mapping documents and ground alignments to establish boundary details for the railway extension.
Technical teams examined physical layout plans across selected sections of the designated corridor. Handheld maps and alignment layouts were evaluated on location to verify site characteristics before further development stages proceed.
The assessment forms part of preliminary field procedures required for land identification and corridor planning. Representatives from both state entities coordinated to cross-check spatial data against actual physical terrain.
The proposed railway line is intended to connect Naivasha to Kisumu and extend further to the border town of Malaba. Planning efforts continue as inter-agency teams complete site verification work across the designated project route.
Further field evaluations and inter-agency consultations are expected to continue as project preparation steps advance. Information regarding the site visit was confirmed through an official social media update published by Kenya Railways Corporation (KRC).

articles.title: Kenya Railways convenes Stakeholders to validate Nairobi Railway City Project - Mjengo Hub
articles.summary: Kenya Railways convenes Stakeholders to validate Nairobi Railway City Project  Mjengo Hub
articles.full_text:
Kenya Railways (KR) has convened public and private sector stakeholders at the Railway Training Institute (RTI) in Nairobi for a validation workshop centered on the Nairobi Railway City (NRC) project. The engagement brought together industry players, urban planners, and government representatives to review and deliberate on the ongoing strategic plans for the transit-oriented development.
The validation workshop was chaired by the Project Manager, who led discussions on the overall framework, technical designs, and operational scope of the major urban infrastructure scheme. Stakeholders reviewed various components of the master plan, examining how the proposed intermodal hub will integrate into Nairobi's existing transport network.
Presentations delivered during the session highlighted key features of the project, including the new Central Station and its surrounding public realm. Project details displayed during the meeting indicated that the new central hub is designed to serve as the primary focal point for multimodal transport across the capital, linking rail, bus, and pedestrian networks.
According to technical materials presented at the workshop, the ongoing revitalization of the Nairobi Commuter Rail (NCR) network aims to significantly expand passenger capacity at Central Station. Current figures indicate that the facility handles approximately 16,000 passengers per day, with operational plans targeting an increase to 30,000 passengers per peak hour upon completion of the redevelopment.
The expanded station design seeks to deliver seamless interconnectivity between multiple transit modes, including Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) lines and non-motorized transport options. Delegates at the workshop discussed the spatial planning requirements necessary to accommodate these higher commuter volumes and support the surrounding commercial and civic spaces.
Kenya Railways (KR) continues to engage technical partners and public agencies as the project moves through its planning and validation stages. Further stakeholder consultations are expected as implementation timelines and structural phases for the multimodal development are finalized.
A version of this report was initially published by Kenya Railways on X.

articles.title: Canada commits up to $180m for Saint John port trade corridor upgrades - Baird Maritime
articles.summary: Canada commits up to $180m for Saint John port trade corridor upgrades  Baird Maritime
articles.full_text:
The Canadian Government has committed up to CA$254 million ($180.7 million) to the Saint John trade corridor project in New Brunswick. The project aims to raise annual container throughput at Port pf Saint John to 850,000 to one million TEU.
Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon announced the funding on October 21 through the trade diversification corridors fund. The provincial government is adding CA$116.5 million and project partners are contributing CA$92.5 million, bringing the combined investment to CA$463 million.
Dredging will widen the port's main channel, and the work also includes breakwater improvements and rehabilitation of marine infrastructure. Transport Canada said the work would add at least 30 per cent to the number of high-water tidal periods during which fully loaded vessels can pass at deeper draughts.
The programme also covers expansion of port warehouses and a new 2,787-square-metre Canada Border Services Agency container examination facility.
Other work includes stabilisation of the Bayshore Rail Terminal shoreline, which protects the port's only rail access, and reconstruction of the Simms Corner intersection to separate rail and road traffic.
New Brunswick Southern Railway will upgrade 103 kilometres of track with continuously welded rail. The upgrade targets mainline speeds of 64 km/h and faster freight journeys connecting the port with Class 1 railways.
Premier Susan Holt said work on the projects could begin in spring 2027 and be completed by 2029 or 2030.
Port Saint John completed its CA$247 million West Side modernisation project in January 2026. Terminal operator DP World said that project and its own investment raised container terminal design capacity from 150,000 TEU to up to one million TEU annually.

articles.title: India's exports to Germany could cross USD 50 billion by 2030: ASSOCHAM - Big News Network.com
articles.summary: India's exports to Germany could cross USD 50 billion by 2030: ASSOCHAM  Big News Network.com
articles.full_text:
New Delhi [India], October 23 (ANI): India's exports of goods and services to Germany could exceed USD 50 billion by 2030, supported by greater use of the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and deeper economic cooperation between the two countries, according to a report by the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India (ASSOCHAM).
The report was released by Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal in Berlin.
The report highlighted the potential for expanding market access, investment and business partnerships between India and Germany. It said the two countries could use their respective strengths in manufacturing, technology and innovation to deepen economic ties and create new growth opportunities.
ASSOCHAM President Nirmal K. Minda said stronger industrial cooperation could help businesses in both countries, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
The India-EU FTA is expected to provide fresh momentum to bilateral trade. According to ASSOCHAM, zero-duty access to a significant share of Indian exports to the European Union could benefit sectors such as textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, gems and jewellery, marine products, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals and electronics.
The report also identified opportunities in advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, digital technology, critical minerals and defence, where Germany's industrial capabilities could complement India's growing manufacturing and services sectors.
ASSOCHAM Secretary General Saurabh Sanyal said green growth was another promising area for cooperation.
He highlighted opportunities linked to Germany's Green and Sustainable Development Partnership and collaboration in renewable energy, green hydrogen, electric mobility and battery storage.
Such cooperation could support investment, technology exchange and sustainable industrial development, he said.
ASSOCHAM Chief Economist S. P. Sharma said India had significant potential to expand exports to Germany through greater utilisation of the India-EU FTA. He said exports could even reach USD 60 billion (EUR 54 billion) by 2030.
The report also stressed the importance of stronger business-to-business engagement, sectoral interactions and buyer-seller meetings to convert the growing economic partnership into concrete commercial opportunities.
Goyal is visiting Germany and the Netherlands from October 22 to 27, leading a delegation of around 100 Indian businesses and startups to explore opportunities in trade, investment and industrial cooperation.
During the visit, he held discussions with German officials and business leaders on expanding bilateral trade, strengthening investment partnerships and increasing cooperation in technology and industry.
ASSOCHAM said it would continue to facilitate industry engagement and knowledge-sharing to help Indian businesses explore opportunities in Germany and strengthen the India-Germany economic partnership. (ANI)

articles.title: WCAF V: African Development Bank Group and UK Export Finance sign MOU to mobilise financing for Africa - African Development Bank Group
articles.summary: WCAF V: African Development Bank Group and UK Export Finance sign MOU to mobilise financing for Africa  African Development Bank Group
articles.full_text:
You are here
WCAF V: African Development Bank Group and UK Export Finance sign MOU to mobilise financing for Africa
The African Development Bank Group (AfDB) and UK Export Finance (UKEF), the United Kingdom’s export credit agency, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen cooperation on co-financing projects across Africa and mobilise additional resources for the continent’s sustainable development.
Abdul Kamara, Officer in Charge, Vice President of the African Development Bank Group, and Tim Reid, Chief Executive of UK Export Finance, signed the agreement on 21 October in Conakry, Guinea, on the sidelines of the fifth UK–West and Central Francophone Africa Trade and Investment Forum (WCAF V). It is the first framework agreement between the two institutions.
“Africa’s financing needs call for partnerships that bring additional capital to the continent at scale. This agreement with UK Export Finance gives our cooperation a structured framework and opens new opportunities to finance the infrastructure and investments that will drive Africa’s growth,” said Abdul Kamara, OIC Vice President of the African Development Bank Group.
The Memorandum of Understanding provides a framework for the two institutions to identify, assess and develop co-financing opportunities for sovereign and non-sovereign operations in the Bank’s regional member countries, drawing on each institution’s financial instruments. The partnership will bring together development finance and export credit to crowd in additional capital for Africa’s strategic investments. Priority areas include energy, infrastructure, water and sanitation, health, digital infrastructure, critical minerals, supply chain resilience, alongside agriculture and trade finance.
“This agreement deepens the relationship between UK Export Finance and the African Development Bank Group. By combining our financial instruments and expertise, we can unlock greater co-financing for the infrastructure, energy and trade priorities that matter most to Africa's growth. UKEF is committed to supporting that ambition, and this partnership will help us do so at greater scale”, said Tim Reid, Chief Executive, UK Export Finance.
The partnership supports the Bank Group’s efforts to mobilise capital at scale, in line with its Four Cardinal Points strategic priorities.
The agreement also reflects the long-standing partnership between the Bank Group and the United Kingdom. The United Kingdom joined the African Development Fund (ADF) in 1973 and became a member of the African Development Bank in 1983. He remains a major contributor to the African Development Fund, which is the Bank Group’s concessional financing window.
The UK Export Finance, established in 1919 as the world’s first export credit agency, provides finance and insurance to support UK businesses and is increasingly active across Africa.

articles.title: Shandong Deepens BRICS Cooperation with Int'l Trade, Investment Conference - The Manila Times
articles.summary: Shandong Deepens BRICS Cooperation with Int'l Trade, Investment Conference  The Manila Times
articles.full_text:
JINAN, China, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The "Dialogue with BRICS - Shandong International Trade and Investment Conference" kicked off on Tuesday in Jinan, the capital of east China's Shandong Province, drawing over 100 business delegates from 30 countries and regions, including BRICS members and partner nations, to meet face-to-face with more than 200 local companies.
Now in its third edition, the event has become a regular fixture on Shandong's business calendar. This year's matchmaking sessions - more than 500 one-on-one meetings - focused on agricultural products, green and low-carbon industries, machinery, high-end chemicals and the digital economy.
Delegates explored cooperation across a wide range of sectors. Ahmed Mustafa Fahmy Hafez, head of the League of Arab States Mission in Beijing, said Arab states are pursuing diversification and see strong potential with Shandong across four areas, namely green energy transition, agricultural and food security, infrastructure and the digital economy, as well as trade and financial innovation. Nahom Berhanu Wendaferew, Minister Counselor at the Embassy of Ethiopia in China, pitched his country's investment potential in agro-processing, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and information and communications technology.
In his keynote speech, Gao Zhikai, deputy director of the Center for China and Globalization (CCG), called for open-source artificial intelligence and international cooperation to boost productivity and deliver shared gains. Zhao Zhongxiu, former president of the University of International Business and Economics, urged Shandong's leading firms to move beyond exporting goods, taking entire industrial chains overseas through technical services and talent development, with priority on equipment manufacturing, green energy, modern agriculture and the marine economy.
Business groups from Malaysia, Indonesia and beyond highlighted opportunities in smart manufacturing and industrial parks, while institutions from non-BRICS members, such as Germany, Serbia and Canada, also leveraged the platform to expand their partnership networks. According to Meide Group, a Shandong-based enterprise, its total shipments to BRICS member states from 2024 through the third quarter of 2026 had reached 1.676 billion yuan (249 million U.S. dollars).
Organized by the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) Shandong Sub-council, the event arrives at a moment of expansion and deepening for the BRICS mechanism, whose member states account for roughly half the world's population, about 30 percent of global GDP and one-fifth of world trade.
Source: CCPIT Shandong Sub-council
